lacuna.name: bisection-champion-pattern
lacuna.repo_anchor: The host already runs the performance-analog of `git bisect run` and names it so in its own sources. vllm_ab_run.py (software/vllm/sm75-marlin/turing_lab/thirdparty/vllm_ab_run.py, 168 lines) opens its docstring: 'Interleaved paired restarts (A,B,A,B,... - the bisect discipline that neutralizes drift), fresh engine per restart, the gate arm protocol per restart, labels asserted, winner gate max(5 percent, 3 sigma)'. Its verdict() is already a three-valued classifier: per-row medians across restarts, gate = max(5.0, 300.0*sigma), verdict in {B_WINS, A_WINS, NO_DIFF} - NO_DIFF is exactly bisect's exit-125 'skip' for a measurement that cannot decide, and the ledger append (ab-champion-ledger.md + ab-ledger.json, with a protocol string in each entry) is the git-bisect-log analog. MEMORY.md 2026-09-10 (window 3): 'the champion-ledger discipline ran end to end... champion A/B an honest NEGATIVE - batching the gather collapses short-decode 78.5 pct (35.4 -> 7.6)... the gather-count thesis is REFUTED... champion stays bridge-gather' and 'A/B withheld per the gate' when gate-0 was 7/8 (the gate refusing to classify is the skip discipline working). MEMORY.md 2026-09-11: 'the variance lived in the per-request python gather loop's engine interaction - not the kernel (bisect-exonerated), not NCCL, not the scheduler' - elimination-by-A/B as causal attribution, and MEMORY.md 2026-08-28 already uses bisect as a verb for kernel debugging plans ('Next session: bisect with a standalone D-fragment dump'). CONSOLIDATION.md final: 'median-of-N discipline MET as standing law (interleaved A/B harness + champion ledger)' and 'the falsification ledger earned equal standing' with 'three causal falsifications (register wall -29 pct, pipeline starvation -44 pct, tile-conditional unroll) map the config-knob space' - the dual-lane mutation ledger is a hand-rolled delta-debugging pass over the config space, with negatives recorded rather than discarded. The weco-cli fork side (weco/local/loop.py, 0.4.0 @ 0111f27e) keeps its own champion as improved_best in append-only steps.jsonl per step (lines 74-85).
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09 the pattern has a 19-year production lineage and a mature academic literature, in five layers. (1) git bisect itself: `git bisect run` automation with the exit-125 skip contract landed 2007-10-27 (commit 71b0251cdd, Christian Couder, 'Bisect run: skip current commit if script exit code is 125', an acknowledged compatibility break that redefined 125 from bad to skip). The contract today, read from git.git master builtin/bisect.c: exit 0 = good, 125 = skip (invokes git bisect skip), 1-124/126/127 = bad, res < 0 or res >= 128 aborts ('bisect run failed: exit code %d... < 0 or >= 128'; exit(-1) chops to 255 via & 0377 and aborts - death by signal aborts). The man page's stated rationale: 125 was chosen as the highest sensible value below the POSIX-shell codes 126 (found but not executable) and 127 (command not found); modern git (present in master 2026; release that introduced it uncertain) adds verify_good: on the FIRST invocation only, a 126/127 result is re-tested on a known-good revision - if the script also exits 126/127 there, 'bogus exit code' aborts the run rather than letting a shell-level script-setup error masquerade as a 'bad' verdict. Bookkeeping is two refs plus a log: refs/bisect/bad and refs/bisect/good-<sha>, with `git bisect log` emitting the session record and `git bisect replay <file>` reconstructing state after reset - the documented mistake-recovery path is log > edit out wrong entries > reset > replay. First-bad-vs-last-good is preserved: the search ends by naming the first bad commit, and when skips make it ambiguous the run stops with 'first bad commit could be any of' (the skip-storm terminal; in C: BISECT_ONLY_SKIPPED_LEFT -> 'bisect run cannot continue any more'). Complexity is log2 (Couder's LK2009 doc shows '10928 revisions left... roughly 14 steps'). (2) The hardening folklore: Couder's 'Fighting regressions with git bisect' (Documentation/git-bisect-lk2009.txt, dated 2009-11-08) documents 'make || exit 125' for broken builds, exit 128-255 as deliberate abort (kill a hung test from outside with a signal), Junio Hamano's perf-regression bisect script (build errors are 'not what I am interested in' -> exit 255, watchdog-style liveness check on the app), merge-base checking when good commits are not ancestors of bad, 'evil merges' as a known attribution hazard, and a 'Bisecting sporadic bugs' section: compiler-dependent non-determinism, the proposed redundancy discipline (re-test an already-classified commit roughly every 3rd step; a mismatching answer aborts early so the operator can fix the log and replay), Ingo Molnar's position that 'even if a bisection fails today it tells us something valuable: it's non-deterministic', and BBChop as the Bayesian alternative. (3) Flaky/noisy bisection research: BBChop (github.com/Ealdwulf/BBChop, Alex Burr, GPL-2.0, experimental - README admits 'it has not found any real bugs, nor has anyone other than me checked the maths') does Bayesian-search-theory bisection tolerant of false negatives but NOT false positives; probe outcomes are Y/N/S(kip), it needs a seeded detection-rate estimate (-n/-p) and a -g logfile for restartable searches, decisions cost O(N). Google industrialized this twice: TeeBeeDee/'tbd' (Dorward et al. 2021, culprit finding for flaky tests at Google) and Flake Aware Culprit Finding (Henderson, Dorward, Nickell, Johnston, Kondareddy, ICST 2023 Industry, DOI 10.1109/ICST57152.2023.00041) - Ben-Or/Hassidim-style noisy binary search over a posterior on every suspect PLUS a no-culprit hypothesis (can answer NONE), live flake-rate re-estimation, priors from the build dependency graph (distance from changed files to the test, historical flake-vs-breakage rates); on 13,600 verified Google breakings (~60% real culprits, ~40% flakes) all FACF variants beat all bisect variants on accuracy (97.5% vs 96.1% for bisect-with-1-rerun), plain k-rerun deflaking plateaus in accuracy while cost grows linearly, and expected-information-gain scheduling showed NO measurable benefit over simple cumulative-median-threshold scheduling - but note its noise model is one-directional (flakes only lie FAIL-on-good, never PASS-on-bad; a half-lie Renyi-Ulam game), whereas performance noise lies both ways. Follow-ups: arXiv 2502.12922 (2025, fault-localization-weighted bisection); Najafi et al. FSE 2019 (simulating bisection with per-commit flaky pass/fail). (4) Delta debugging and reduction: ddmin (Zeller 1999 ESEC/FSE; Zeller & Hildebrandt, IEEE TSE 28(2) 2002, 'Simplifying and Isolating Failure-Inducing Input') - granularity-doubling partition/complement search producing a 1-minimal test case in worst-case quadratic tests (best ~log n), plus the isolation variant that finds the minimal failure-inducing DIFFERENCE between two inputs; a TSE retrospective appeared in 2025. HDD (Misherghi & Su ICSE 2006) does the same over a grammar tree; Hodovan et al. 2016 cut test counts at equal minimality; C-Reduce (Regehr's lab, PLDI 2012 companion paper; creduce man page) is the robustness lesson: the interestingness predicate is an exit-code contract (0 = interesting), must be wrapped in a timeout (built-in default 300s; timed-out subcommands should exit 124; 'timeouts must not occur too often or else C-Reduce will work poorly'), should be deterministic - but the PLDI paper concedes compiler predicates are often neither monotone nor deterministic and the reducer degrades gracefully rather than failing; --also-interesting archives near-miss variants. Perses (ICSE 2017) gains robustness by construction (validity-preserving transformations); llvm-reduce is the LLVM descendant; `opt -opt-bisect-limit=N` (LLVM docs) is bisection applied one level down (which optimization pass). (5) Performance bisection where good/bad becomes better/worse-in-noise: Chromium's bisect-perf-regression.py (catapult, now removed) was replaced by Pinpoint, whose compare.py is the canonical noise-band classifier: per-commit repeat Attempts, Mann-Whitney U AND Kolmogorov-Smirnov with p = min(both) ('MWU is bad at detecting changes in variance, and K-S is bad with discrete distributions. So use both'), dynamic low/high thresholds with functional floors 0.05/0.10, four statuses DIFFERENT / SAME / UNKNOWN / PENDING where UNKNOWN explicitly means 'collect more data before making a final decision' - the statistical skip; docs tell engineers to distrust a culprit 'well within the noise' and re-bisect. The academic backing is Ocariza, 'On the Effectiveness of Bisection in Performance Regression Localization' (EMSE 27:95, 2022, DOI 10.1007/s10664-022-10152-3; 310 perf bug reports analyzed): bisection stays highly effective for perf regressions but effectiveness is sensitive to configuration - repetition counts and classification thresholds - because perf verdicts are 'neither binary nor monotonic due to the noise inherent in performance measurements' (detailed per-config numbers not retrieved [uncertain: ocariza-emse22-detailed-numbers]). Mozilla's equivalents: mozregression (build-level bisect with custom automatic eval scripts) and MozillaSecurity/autobisect (active, MPL-2.0): --repeat N evaluates the testcase N times per build for flaky repros, --ignore timeout,memory,log-limit filters noisy outcome classes so they do not count as reproductions, per-iteration --timeout (60s default) and --launch-timeout (300s), 30GB build cache. Racing/irace is the campaign-scale answer: F-Race (Birattari et al. 2002) and irace (Lopez-Ibanez, Dubois-Lacoste, Stutzle, Birattari, Operations Research Perspectives 3:43-58, 2016) evaluate candidate configurations in parallel on instances and statistically eliminate (Friedman rank test) as soon as a candidate is significantly worse - champion-vs-challenger with a statistical gate as the primary loop, sampling new candidates biased toward elites. Fault-localization transfers when attribution must go broader than a chain: Tarantula (Jones/Harrold/Stasko ICSE 2002), Ochiai (Abreu/Zoeteweij/van Gemund QSIC 2006 - the coefficient that keeps topping SBFL evaluations), statistical debugging (Liblit et al. PLDI 2005), and cause transitions (Cleve & Zeller ICSE 2005) rank suspects from pass/fail spectra over MANY runs instead of assuming a monotone boundary - the principled version of the host's mutation ledger.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers to the weco-local long-range runner and the turing_lab A/B harness concretely. (1) The verdict enum, not the boolean: git's contract survived 19 years because it has exactly four outcomes - good / bad / skip / abort - with the abort class kept SEPARATE from bad (exit >= 128, and 126/127 sanity-checked against a known-good revision before being trusted). vllm_ab_run.py's verdict() already has the good/bad/skip thirds (A_WINS/B_WINS/NO_DIFF); the missing fourth is the abort class - a timed-out or crashed measurement must never be classified as data (it is neither NO_DIFF nor a loss for the challenger); that half belongs to the sibling unattended-loop item, and this item supplies the classification discipline it should feed. (2) verify_good transfers verbatim as the incumbent calibration run: git's defense against shell-level 126/127 masquerading as 'bad' is to re-run the suspect script on a known-good commit; the champion analog is to periodically re-run the INCUMBENT arm and check it still lands inside its banked band - a flipped incumbent measurement is the signature of drift/poisoned cache/the founding-variance problem, and it should quarantine the session (re-baseline) rather than dethrone the champion on bad evidence. (3) UNKNOWN-then-collect (Pinpoint) upgrades the fixed max(5 pct, 3 sigma) gate into an adaptive one: after each paired A/B restart run a two-sample rank test (Mann-Whitney U is distribution-free and matches medians) plus the existing magnitude floor; if p lands between low and high, add ONE more paired restart and recompute, capped at R attempts; a capped-out comparison records NO_DIFF with n and p attached. This spends GPU time only where the verdict is genuinely undecided - the same economy irace gets from early elimination of clear winners/losers. (4) The ledger IS bisect-log: keep it append-only and make standings replayable from the ledger alone (recompute champion from entries); a wrong verdict is then repaired git-style - append a correcting entry, never edit history (already the host's MEMORY discipline). (5) The skip-storm guard: git stops with 'first bad commit could be any of' when skips destroy the boundary; the campaign analog is to count consecutive/aggregate NO_DIFF-with-held verdicts and treat a rising skip rate as a signal about the MEASUREMENT (Pinpoint: 'within the noise'; FACF: bound flake rates, skip tests >50% flaky), not as data about the candidates. (6) Falsification ledger = ddmin's negatives: keep recording REFUTED theses with mechanism (gather-count, W4A16 pipeline, tile-unroll); when a champion is found, a ddmin-style 1-minimality pass over the winning diff (drop each env flag/hunk, re-gate, keep only deltas that preserve the win) yields the smallest honest champion and the cheapest reproducible evidence. (7) When attribution must go beyond a chain (interaction effects, config-knob space), spectra beat bisection: rank knobs/lanes by an Ochiai-style suspiciousness over the accumulated A/B and mutation-lane outcomes instead of running more pairwise bisects - the dual-lane mutation ledger is already this pattern hand-rolled. Does NOT transfer: git's DAG machinery (merge-base verification, first-parent mode, refs/bisect/*) - the campaign's candidate space is a config/patch lattice, not a commit DAG, and perf noise is symmetric where BBChop and FACF both assume one-directional lies, so their posteriors need a two-error-rate generalization before reuse [uncertain: two-sided-noisy-search-transfer]; C-Reduce's language-specific transformation passes (no equivalent corpus here); Pinpoint's fleet/App-Engine infrastructure (two local GPUs); full FACF Bayesian machinery while the campaign is 2-candidate A/B rather than N-suspect culprit finding - its useful residue at this scale is the no-culprit hypothesis (the verdict 'the harness is broken, no champion' must exist) and the measured result that info-gain scheduling buys nothing over a simple threshold.

design.mechanism: Cold-implementable contract, four pieces. (A) Four-valued verdict in vllm_ab_run.py: after each paired restart i, collect per-row values; per deciding row compute Mann-Whitney U p-value between arm A and arm B samples (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu, exact for small n; no new heavyweight deps beyond scipy); classify: WIN/LOSS when p <= low AND |delta_pct| > gate (gate stays max(5.0, 300*sigma)); UNKNOWN when low < p <= high (low=0.05, high=0.10, Pinpoint's floors) OR |delta_pct| <= gate while p <= low; DONE-SAME (NO_DIFF) when p > high. On UNKNOWN: schedule one more paired restart (A,B) - interleaving is what kills drift - recompute from the concatenated samples, cap at R restarts (default 4); on cap, verdict NO_DIFF with {n, p, delta_pct} attached. On harness failure/timeout of either arm: verdict ABORT for the pair, retry the pair once, then stop the comparison (never convert an ABORT into NO_DIFF or a loss). (B) Ledger schema (append-only, ab-ledger.json plus markdown mirror): entry = {ts, arm_a, arm_b, restarts: [{arm, rows, wall_s, exit}], verdict, n, p, delta_pct, gate_pct, evidence: [gate log paths], replaces: null | prior-entry-id}. Champion standings are DERIVED: a function fold(ledger) -> current champion per lane; replay = run fold on a fresh checkout of the ledger file (the git-bisect-log property: the log alone reconstructs the search state). (C) Incumbent calibration tripwire (verify_good analog): every K-th comparison entry (default 3), the incumbent arm re-runs solo against its own banked band; if the incumbent's median exits [banked_median +/- max(5 pct, 3*banked_sigma)], set session_state = QUARANTINE: no further verdicts recorded, operator alert with the divergence row, re-baseline before resuming (this catches drift/poisoned state - the founding-variance class - before it contaminates standings). (D) Skip-rate and no-culprit guards: counters for consecutive NO_DIFF and consecutive ABORT; consecutive NO_DIFF >= 2 or aggregate skip rate > 50 pct => stop scheduling new challengers, report 'measurement undecidable' (FACF: do not keep racing a >50 pct flaky test); consecutive ABORT >= 3 => campaign abort (the probe driver's existing heuristic). (E) Champion minimization pass (optional, run on adoption): for each env flag / code hunk in the winning diff, flip it off and re-run a single gated comparison; keep only deltas whose removal changes the verdict (1-minimality, ddmin); every removal that does NOT change the verdict is recorded in the falsification ledger with its delta_pct. All exits through the existing append-only JSONL surfaces so the sibling watchdog item's heartbeat monitoring sees progress unchanged.
design.failure_modes: Documented in the wild, with defenses. (1) Non-deterministic verdicts flip the search: git docs route flakiness through skip; FACF quantifies that k-rerun deflaking plateaus in accuracy while cost grows linearly, and a single wrong 'bad' can send the whole search down the wrong half. Defense: three-part - adaptive UNKNOWN (spend repetitions only when undecided), the incumbent tripwire (catches environment drift before standings rot), and recording n/p/delta on every verdict so a later reader can re-judge. (2) Skip-storms: git's terminal 'first bad commit could be any of' / 'bisect run cannot continue any more' when skips destroy the boundary; skip is not free - it discards information. Defense: skip-rate counters with a stop-and-report rule (measurement undecidable), and prefer spending one more paired restart over skipping when budget allows. (3) Monotonicity violation (the deep one): bisection and ddmin both assume the bad set is downward-closed / the predicate monotone; merge semantics ('evil merges', LK2009), interaction bugs, and perf configs violate it - the culprit of a combination is in neither parent alone, and ddmin formalizes this as needing complement probes. Defense: when a pairwise chain keeps returning contradictions (incumbent tripwire fires but re-baseline is clean), switch attribution mode from chain-bisect to spectra: Ochiai-style ranking over ALL accumulated lane outcomes (the mutation ledger), which makes no monotonicity assumption. (4) Predicate quality (creduce man page): interestingness must be cheap, timeout-wrapped (exit 124 for timeout), and near-deterministic; 'timeouts must not occur too often or the reducer works poorly'. Defense: gate-0 triangulation before any A/B (the host's existing gate arm protocol), hard wall-clock per arm, and ABORT classification so poisoned runs never masquerade as verdicts. (5) Early termination on a wrong champion: BBChop warns an over-high initial detection-rate estimate terminates early at a wrong location; Pinpoint floors its thresholds (0.05/0.10) precisely so cheap p-values cannot reach significance with too few samples. Defense: keep the magnitude floor ON TOP of significance (a real but 0.1 pct difference must not dethrone a champion), floor the p thresholds, cap-free UNKNOWN escalation only within R. (6) Asymmetric-noise models silently misapplied: FACF/BBChop assume tests only lie in one direction (false FAIL); performance noise lies both ways. Defense: use two-sample symmetric tests (Mann-Whitney over paired restarts) rather than importing their likelihood tables; the tripwire provides the empirical two-sided alarm. (7) The search itself corrupts the system under test (fresh-engine-per-restart exists for this): keep restart-level isolation; a champion adopted after an interleaved run must re-baseline its OWN band from its own restarts (banked numbers come from the run that crowned it, not from the older incumbent's).
design.effort_estimate: Wrapper-level only, no weco-fork change required. (1) vllm_ab_run.py: UNKNOWN/adaptive-restart verdict loop + p-value + counters (~60 lines; mannwhitneyu needs scipy, present via the vLLM dependency set, and a hand-rolled rank-sum U is a ~15-line fallback if not); (2) ledger replay/fold + schema fields (~40 lines python); (3) incumbent calibration tripwire + quarantine flag (~25 lines); (4) champion minimization pass as a separate small script reusing run_restart (~50 lines, optional); (5) doctrine: runbook amendment defining verdict classes, skip-rate stop rules, and quarantine handling (prose only). The ABORT-vs-skip classification hooks are already provided by the sibling supervision item's timeout/retry work; this item defines what the classifier does with those signals.
design.priority_signal: For: this is the campaign's standing law, not an option - CONSOLIDATION's final status names 'median-of-N discipline MET as standing law (interleaved A/B harness + champion ledger)' and 'the falsification ledger earned equal standing', so the verdict classifier is load-bearing every window; the two failure classes that actually cost this host GPU days (the founding 9-27 pct variance question, closed only by elimination across four windows, and authoring bugs like the splits-cap silent-coverage defect) are precisely the classes this lineage hardened against - drift detection (tripwire), undecidable gates (UNKNOWN), and wrong-verdict recovery (append-only replayable ledger); and the pattern is 19 years of upstream production hardening (git 2007, Chromium, Google) available for ~150 lines of local code, with every piece having a cited precedent rather than a novel design. Against: the campaign today is 2-candidate A/B with a human at window open/close, not unattended N-suspect culprit finding - full Bayesian machinery (FACF) would be overfit; the adaptive-restart escalation costs extra GPU time exactly on the marginal comparisons, which on a 10h window is real money; the magnitude-vs-significance subtlety means a mis-set floor can either waste restarts or let 1 pct noise through, so the floor values need one calibration window; and the incumbent tripwire duplicates some coverage the gate-0 triangulation already provides (it catches code bugs, not environment drift - the tripwire's unique value). Net: land the four-valued verdict + ledger replay + tripwire now (they are small, precedent-backed, and every future window uses them); defer the minimization pass and any posterior-based scheduling; revisit FACF-style machinery only if campaigns go multi-candidate per lane.
